Byomkesh.description: The central detective of the story, known as a 'truth-seeker' or 'satyanweshi', who investigates the porcupine quill murders.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, often present during investigations.

Rakhalbabu.description: A police inspector who collaborates with Byomkesh on the murder cases.

Debashish.description: Owner of Butterfly Cosmetics, recently married to Dipa, and a target of the porcupine quill attacks.

Dipa.description: Debashish's young wife, previously in love with another man, caught in a difficult marriage.

Nakul.description: The loyal cook and servant in Debashish's household, privy to the family's daily life.

Nripati.description: A well-educated widower who hosts regular tea and chat sessions for local young men.

Bijoy.description: Dipa's older brother, involved in arranging her marriage and protective of family honor.

Nil Madhav.description: Dipa's father, a college professor, upholding traditional family values.

Uday Madhav Mukherjee.description: Dipa's grandfather, former college principal and family patriarch, paralyzed and authoritative.

Probal.description: A musician, singer, and childhood acquaintance of Debashish, later revealed as the murderer.

Kapil.description: A wealthy, educated bachelor with an interest in astronomy and part of Nripati's circle.

Kharga Bahadur.description: A famous football player of Nepali-Bengali heritage, member of the tea session group.

Sujan Mitra.description: A rising film actor, known for his good looks and level-headedness, part of the friend group.

Shubhra.description: Dipa's close friend, a jovial and married woman who visits her after the wedding.

Padmalochan.description: The elderly gardener hired to help Dipa with her new garden.

Dr Ramprasad Dutta.description: The seniormost chemist at Butterfly Cosmetics, respected by Dipa and Debashish.

Dr Gupta.description: The hospital doctor who treats Debashish after the porcupine quill attack.

Dinanath.description: Nripati’s loyal valet, also called Dinu, who assists with household affairs and is trusted by the family.

Ratan Singh.description: Kharga Bahadur’s valet and cook, responsible for preparing kebabs.

Ramola.description: Kapil’s sister-in-law, who manages the household and is known for her sharp temperament.

Ashoka.description: Kapil’s elder sister, married to Sailenbabu, with a son at boarding school.

Sailenbabu.description: Kapil’s brother-in-law, a talkative and argumentative man.

Dr Surit Sen.description: The physician who attends Dipa’s family and treats Debashish during his illness.

Satyaboti.description: Appears in the epilogue as a listener to Byomkesh’s explanation.

Calcutta.description: The city in which the story is set, now known as Kolkata.

Gol Park.description: A well-known landmark and traffic circle in south Calcutta.

Rabindra Sarobar.description: A large lake and park area in south Calcutta, site of several murders.

Garia.description: A neighborhood in south Calcutta, where Gunamoybabu lives.

Keyatala.description: A locality in south Calcutta where Byomkesh resides.

Utpala theatre.description: A cinema hall in Calcutta mentioned as showing a film.

Butterfly Cosmetics.description: The cosmetics factory owned by Debashish.

Delhi.description: The capital city of India, where Debashish studied.

University of Delhi.description: A prestigious university where Debashish stayed with a professor.

Sandilya.description: A Brahmin gotra (clan lineage) mentioned in the context of Debashish's sacred thread ceremony.

Banerjee.description: A common Bengali Brahmin surname, also used as a gotra reference.

Chatterjee.description: A Bengali Brahmin surname, mentioned in the context of caste.

Ballygunge.description: A prominent neighborhood in south Calcutta.

Maiden.description: Refers to the Maidan, a large urban park in central Calcutta.

New Market.description: A famous shopping area in central Calcutta.

Dum Dum.description: A locality in Calcutta, mentioned as a site for music recording.

Southern Avenue.description: A major road in south Calcutta, bordering Rabindra Sarobar.

Bangalore.description: A major city in southern India, mentioned as a travel destination.

Kathmandu.description: The capital of Nepal, referenced in connection with Kharga Bahadur's postponed marriage.

Nepal.description: Country of origin for Kharga Bahadur's family.

Sindhi.description: An ethnic group from Sindh, referenced as one of Kharga Bahadur’s guests.

Punjabi.description: An ethnic group from Punjab, referenced as one of Kharga Bahadur’s guests.

Parsi.description: A Zoroastrian community in India, referenced as one of Kharga Bahadur’s guests.

Darjeeling.description: A hill station in West Bengal, where Kapil’s sister and her husband live.

Rashbehari Hospital.description: The hospital where Debashish is taken after the attack.

Shojarur Kanta.description: The original Bengali title of the story, meaning 'The Quills of the Porcupine'.

Gita.description: Refers to the Bhagavad Gita, a sacred Hindu scripture.

Rabindranath Tagore.description: A Nobel laureate Bengali poet and composer, whose songs are performed in the story.

D.L. Roy.description: A Bengali poet and composer, referenced in Dipa’s bookshelf.

Nazrul.description: Refers to Kazi Nazrul Islam, a renowned Bengali poet and musician.

Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.description: A famous Bengali novelist, referenced by Byomkesh.

Govinda Das.description: A Bengali poet, quoted by Shubhra.

Krishna.description: A Hindu deity, referenced in a poetic couplet.

Saraswati.description: The Hindu goddess of knowledge and arts, represented by a silver idol gifted to Dipa.

Agfa.description: A brand of photographic film and envelopes, used to store Sujan’s photograph.

Ovaltine.description: A malted drink, given to Debashish in the hospital.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment for men, a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

kurta.description: A traditional Indian long shirt worn by men.

puri.description: A deep-fried Indian bread, often served with curry.

kachori.description: A deep-fried snack filled with spiced lentils or vegetables.

dal pakora.description: A fried snack made from lentil batter.

esraj.description: A stringed musical instrument from Bengal, played with a bow.

gotra.description: A Hindu lineage or clan assigned at birth.

horoscope.description: An astrological chart used in Indian matchmaking.

purdah.description: The practice of secluding women from public observation, common in traditional Indian families.
